**Discpress 1.8.0 is the dependable one**: the fixes from a full review of the app. No finished result gets lost, no disc takes another game's tracks or name, and big folders of games are added quickly.

## Get it

- **[⬇ discpress.html](https://github.com/PowerBeef/discpress/releases/download/v1.8.0/discpress.html)** (about 3 MB): the whole app in one file you keep. If you use the downloaded file, download it again for this version.
- **[🌐 powerbeef.github.io/discpress](https://powerbeef.github.io/discpress/)**: nothing to download, and the way to convert big games on iPhone and iPad. It updates itself.

## The right tracks, the right name

- **A cue sheet or GDI added on its own** no longer takes the tracks of another game in a folder you add next. Every Dreamcast game's first track is called `track01.bin`, so this was easy to hit.
- **Some Sega discs have a serial number Redump lists only without its ending** (T-25406H-1). Such a disc is no longer named after another game with the same base serial (T-25406H is Hexen, T-25406H-50 is Doom). The card offers that name with **Use this name**, and you decide.
- **A serial found only in a shortened form** names nothing when the release is for another region.
- **File names with accents** match their cue sheet even when they're written the way macOS writes them.
- **A cue sheet with an unquoted name such as `Tony's Game.bin`** now converts. Before, it reported a missing file.
- **Two lines of a cue sheet naming one file in different case** (`Twine.bin`, `twine.bin`) no longer leave the card waiting for a file that's there.
- **PlayStation 2:** these discs are now identified correctly:
  - discs without `BOOT2` in their `SYSTEM.CNF`;
  - games Redump lists both on CD and on DVD, where the disc itself decides.
- **Better recognition of other discs:**
  - a PC disc with a `VIDEO_TS` folder is no longer called a video disc;
  - Super Video CDs are recognized;
  - Saturn discs of sets of ten or more are read correctly (`CD-10/12`).
- **cdrdao `.toc` discs** get the same emulator notes as cue sheets.
- **A cue sheet that misses `INDEX 01`'s leading zero** (`INDEX 1`) is identified.
- **PlayStation discs with LibCrypt:**
  - a CloneCD `.sub` inside a zip is used;
  - a `.sub` or `.sbi` is kept when you remove a card and add the game again, or when a cue sheet takes over its `.bin`;
  - a 2,048-byte `.bin` gets the warning that it lost data.

## Nothing lost

- **Run again** asks before it throws away a result you haven't saved, as every other button does.
- **Save all to a folder** never lets two results of the same name replace each other. The second is left for you to save on its own.
- **When the browser's storage fails**, the page asks before keeping a big result in memory, rather than risk losing it.
- **A save into a folder that fails** removes every file it had started, so no cue sheet is left without its tracks.
- **In Chrome and Edge, results of 1 GB or more** are saved through the system's Save dialog. If you cancel it, the result stays unsaved, where a canceled download used to count as saved.
- **Results from your last visit** show **✓ Saved** once you save them.
- **When results are kept in memory**, the question asked before a big job counts what an ECM image, a PBP disc or a compressed ISO holds, not its packed size.
- **A damaged CloneCD `.ccd` file** can no longer freeze the page.

## Big folders, quickly

- **Adding thousands of files** at once is faster: 10,000 files take about 14 seconds instead of 24, nearly all of it spent reading the files.
- **Removing a card while it's being identified** stops its checksum, so the next card goes on at once.
- **A zip added again** says it's already in the list.
- **A multi-disc `EBOOT.PBP` added again** after you removed one disc brings back only that disc.

## Advanced tab

- **Adding a file with the same name** as one in the list says that it replaced it.
- **A cue sheet chdman can't read as it is** points you to the Convert tab, which corrects it.
- **The compression you picked** stays when you change the type of CHD.

## Steadier

- **Verify:**
  - stops when its card is reset, removed or cleared;
  - its verdict never lands on a newer run;
  - for a result saved in a folder, it reads the folder the result is in.
- **A card no longer stays at "Identifying game…"** after an error, and doesn't wait for a DAT check it doesn't need. One failed DAT check no longer stops the others.
- **The screen stays awake only while jobs run.**
- **The online version always answers when offline**, even when the browser's cache fails.
- **A broken record from an earlier visit** or a broken saved setting no longer stops the page from starting.
- **Answers from helper threads are checked**, so a WebAssembly engine that miscompiles can't write a damaged CHD. An extract whose helper threads all failed finishes on one thread.
- **Extracting a CD with the cue sheet kept:**
  - a cue sheet whose track types don't match the disc's is no longer written back;
  - a cue sheet, GDI or TOC that couldn't be written is reported as an error.
- **The game database** lists a release once with all its serial numbers: 20% fewer rows, the same names.
- **Every release** ships only a commit whose tests passed.

CHDs are the same as 1.7.1's, byte for byte the same as chdman 0.289's with the default settings.
